title: Evaluate the Exact Serving Build
summary: This intermediate module enables you to distinguish artifact identity from behavioral similarity. After completing it, you can compare immutable artifact identifiers, document the result, and avoid treating a successful behavior check as proof that two serving builds are identical.
objectives: Compare the digest, size, and media type recorded for a reference artifact and a candidate artifact.
Determine whether available evidence establishes that two references identify the same packaged content.
Explain why matching test outputs do not by themselves prove artifact identity.
Document an exact-build evaluation without relying on a mutable label.

sections.title: Currency correction
paragraphs: The previous citation, content/modules/self-hosted-model-operations/evaluate-the-exact-serving-build.json, had an unregistered publisher and had never been verified. It has been removed and replaced with the official descriptor specification maintained by the Open Container Initiative.

This source change affects the support for claims about immutable artifact identity. The corrected material now limits those claims to the digest, size, and media type defined by the cited specification. Unsupported provider-specific procedures, tool instructions, version requirements, and configuration details are omitted. The correction is limited to the citation and the artifact-identification guidance it supports.

sections.title: Intermediate scope and terms
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes that you understand the basic difference between deploying packaged content and sending a request to that deployed content. It does not assume familiarity with a particular provider or implementation.

In this module, a reference is the packaged artifact you intend to reproduce, and a candidate is the packaged artifact being evaluated. A digest is a content-addressed identifier calculated from bytes. A media type identifies the format of the referenced content, and size records its byte length.

An exact-build evaluation asks an identity question: does the candidate reference the same packaged content as the reference? A behavior check asks a different question: do the two deployments produce the expected results for selected inputs? These questions require separate conclusions.

sections.title: Compare immutable artifact identifiers
paragraphs: Obtain the descriptor for the reference artifact and the descriptor for the candidate artifact from the records available in the serving process. Record the digest, size, and media type from each descriptor. Do not substitute a mutable label for the digest.

Compare digest with digest, size with size, and media type with media type. If the digests differ, the descriptors do not identify the same packaged content. If the digests match, the digest evidence identifies the same content. Matching size alone is insufficient because different content can have the same byte length.

Keep the conclusion limited to what was compared. A digest for one referenced artifact does not establish the identity of data or runtime inputs stored outside that artifact. Any external input needed for the evaluation must be identified and compared separately before making a broader exact-serving-build claim.
sections.callout: Artifact identity is established from immutable identifiers, not from a familiar name or from similar observed behavior.

sections.title: Separate identity evidence from behavior evidence
paragraphs: Run any behavior check as a separate validation step. Use the same recorded inputs and the same evaluation rule for the reference and candidate so that the comparison itself does not change between runs.

A passing behavior check shows only that the observed results met the chosen rule for the tested inputs. It does not prove that the packaged artifacts are identical. Conversely, an artifact-identity match does not by itself state that an external service, external data source, or other input behaved identically.

Report two conclusions when both checks are performed: an artifact-identity conclusion based on descriptor comparison and a behavior conclusion based on the recorded test. This separation prevents behavioral similarity from being presented as proof of build identity.

sections.title: Record the decision
paragraphs: For an auditable result, record the reference descriptor values, candidate descriptor values, comparison outcome, date of evaluation, and scope of the conclusion. If an expected descriptor value is unavailable, record that the exact identity was not established rather than guessing it.

A defensible statement is: the reference and candidate descriptors have matching digest, size, and media type, so the available descriptor evidence identifies the same packaged content. If external inputs were not compared, state that limitation explicitly.
After this module, you can perform and explain a provider-neutral artifact-identity comparison that you could not perform from a mutable label or behavior check alone.

questions.prompt: The reference and candidate descriptors contain different digests. What conclusion is supported?
choices: They identify the same packaged content because their labels match.
They do not identify the same packaged content.
They are identical if one behavior check passes.
Their identity is established by matching size alone.
questions.explanation: The module states that different digests do not identify the same packaged content. Labels, behavior checks, and size alone do not override that result.

questions.prompt: Two deployments pass the same behavior check. What does that result establish by itself?
choices: Their observed results met the chosen rule for the tested inputs.
Their descriptors must contain matching digests.
questions.explanation: A behavior check supports a conclusion about the observed results under that check. Artifact identity requires a separate comparison of immutable identifiers.

questions.prompt: Which set of descriptor values should be compared for the reference and candidate?
questions.explanation: The module directs the learner to record and compare digest, size, and media type for both descriptors.

questions.prompt: What changed during this currency correction?
choices: A named provider procedure was added.
The unverified local citation was replaced with an official descriptor specification, affecting support for artifact-identity guidance.
Behavior checks were redefined as proof of artifact identity.
A required implementation version was introduced.
questions.explanation: The currency section states that the unverified local citation was replaced and that the change affected support for claims about immutable artifact identity.
